sets.note: Inputs: altitude m, turbidity, Rayleigh sea-level density. Rayleigh is Taichi's; Mie is the fit to Elterman's profile (mie_density_reference) in place of the original's plateau; ozone is the number density (m^-3) of the measured profile (ozone_density_reference) in place of the original's analytic shape.

Inputs: wavelength nm, turbidity. Outputs: Rayleigh, Mie per metre at unit density; ozone cross section in m^2 (ozone_extinction_reference), the original's nearest-lower lookup times its fixed number density replaced. n*n - 1 for air (n ~ 1.0003) keeps ~3e-4 relative f32 rounding, which an FMA contraction removes, hence the relative tolerance; every value is far from 0.

Inputs: cos_theta, g, alpha. Outputs: Rayleigh, HG(g), Klein-Nishina(3000), Draine(g, alpha), cloud, cloud with reduced peak. The relative tolerance covers f32 cancellation in 1 + g^2 - 2 g cos near the forward peak.
Inputs: u xyz, view. Outputs: HG(0.8), Klein-Nishina(3000), cloud, cloud with reduced peak. The Draine inversion loses about 1e-3 in f32.

Inputs: u xyz, view. Outputs: HG(0.8), Klein-Nishina(3000), cloud, cloud with reduced peak. u at 0 or 1 sends cos_theta to +-1, where sin_theta = sqrt(1 - cos^2) amplifies f32 rounding of the inversions to ~1e-2.
Inputs: r, mu, mu_s, nu. Outputs: u_nu, u_mu_s, u_mu, u_r, intersects_ground. mu_s below -0.2 maps to the domain edge.
r within 100 m of the ground: r*r - R*R cancels in f32, so u_r and the ground half of u_mu carry ~1e-2 of rounding noise in the original too.
Outputs: r, mu, mu_s, nu, intersects_ground. The absolute tolerance covers f32 cancellation in the cosines near the horizon; r is relative.
Outputs: mu, r (the original returns r - planet radius). The bake evaluates texel centres (fix 8); the corner rows are the original's x / RES grid.
